subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Untyped `any` cast (`stackSdk: Stack as any`) with no explanatory comment, violating strict-TS review criterion 1. The package exports the exact type this cast is faking: `@contentstack/live-preview-utils` re-exports `IStackSdk` (verified in dist/modern/index.d.ts: `export { type IStackSdk, ContentstackLivePreview as default }`), whose shape (`{ live_preview: {...} & Partial<IConfig>; environment: string; [key: string]: any }`) the contentstack Stack instance satisfies structurally.
issues.suggestedFix: Import the type and cast through it: `import ContentstackLivePreview, { type IStackSdk } from '@contentstack/live-preview-utils'` then `stackSdk: Stack as unknown as IStackSdk` — or, if Stack already satisfies IStackSdk, pass it without a cast. If a cast proves unavoidable, add an explanatory comment per criterion 1.

issues.description: The onEntryChange handler resolves the changed entry by scraping the DOM: `document.querySelector('[data-cslp]')` returns the FIRST tagged element anywhere on the page (header, footer, nav, shared components all carry cslp tags), then casts the fetched result to IContentstackPage and pushes it into previewPage, which overrides `page` for every useContent consumer via effectiveContent. If the first data-cslp element belongs to a non-page entry (e.g. header), the entire page context is replaced with a header entry and the Homepage/Article render breaks — precisely the pages the ACs target. The handler also silently returns when no tagged element exists, so changes to untagged content never preview. This is fragile hand-rolled plumbing where the SDK already delivers change events (onEntryChange is the documented subscription point in light-sdk.d.ts).
issues.suggestedFix: Use the entry change payload/config from `ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange` (the SDK's own mechanism) rather than scanning the DOM for the first `[data-cslp]` node; at minimum, scope the query to the page entry's content type (the page's own contentTypeUid, already available as pageProps.contentTypeUid in MyApp) and only setPreviewPage when the fetched entry's content type matches the current page — never blindly cast an arbitrary first-match entry to IContentstackPage.

issues.description: Deviation from the plan of record: useContent.ts was explicitly marked NO EDIT REQUIRED, and the prescribed design was to add an updater (setContent/updatePage) to IContentstackContext so ContentstackContext itself becomes reactive — in which case useContent's existing useCallback dependency on `content` re-renders all 147+ consumers with zero changes to this file. Instead a parallel LivePreviewContext was added and useContent was edited to merge previewPage over content on every render. This works, but it is more machinery than prescribed (new context interface, new provider, hook edit, `{...content, page: previewPage}` allocation per render) and touches a file the plan froze.
issues.suggestedFix: Prefer the prescribed shape: hold the (possibly preview-updated) page in state inside the provider that feeds ContentstackContext.Provider and expose an updater on IContentstackContext; then useContent needs no edit and no second context. If the parallel-context approach is retained intentionally, note the deviation — it is functionally equivalent but not the plan of record.

issues.description: Endpoint URL `api.contentstack.io` is hardcoded as a fallback string literal (criterion 6 prefers named constants). Note this duplicates the SDK's own built-in default (contentstack bundle: `live_preview:{enable:!1,host:"api.contentstack.io"}`), so the fallback adds nothing when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is unset. Also verified: the installed contentstack SDK's LivePreview type (index.d.ts:123) requires `management_token`, not the `preview_token` named in the root-cause analysis — passing CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN as management_token matches the installed SDK contract, so that deviation from the RCA is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the `|| "api.contentstack.io"` fallback and only set `host` when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is provided (`...(CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST ? { host: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST } : {})`), letting the SDK default apply; or hoist the URL into a named constant.

issues.description: Empty catch block swallows all fetch errors with only a comment. If the preview re-fetch fails (network, bad token), the author sees stale preview state with no signal, making preview issues undebuggable.
issues.suggestedFix: Log the error (console.warn or the project's existing logger) before preserving prior state.

issues.description: `previewPage?: [IContentstackPage]` uses a fixed-length tuple type for what is semantically an array of one page; `[IContentstackPage] | undefined` is awkward to construct and destructure. `setPreviewPage` is also exposed on the context although no consumer outside the provider needs it (useContent only reads previewPage).
issues.suggestedFix: Type as `IContentstackPage[] | undefined` (or `IContentstackPage | undefined` since only one page is ever set) and expose only `previewPage` on the context value.

issues.description: `ContentstackLivePreview.init({ enable: true, ... })` runs unconditionally in all environments (production included). The live-preview SDK only activates when a preview hash/postMessage is present, so behavior is safe, but initializing it on every page load for every user is unnecessary work and surface area. SPEC advisory: the verification criterion for protected/gated pages ('draft content must not render in a protected state') is not addressed anywhere in the plan of record or this diff — the plan names no gating site, so this is a gap in the spec to raise with the story owner, not the implementer.
issues.suggestedFix: Gate init on the presence of a preview indicator (e.g. only initialize when the live_preview hash query param is present or NODE_ENV !== 'production'), and flag the protected-page criterion to the story owner as unplanned scope.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The onEntryChange handler determines which entry changed by scraping document.querySelector('[data-cslp]'), which returns the FIRST editable element in the DOM — not the entry that actually changed. On the MX Homepage (header, footer, hero banner, and mapped components all carry data-cslp tags), this will typically resolve to a header/footer or arbitrary component entry, whose fetch result is then cast to IContentstackPage and pushed into previewPage, replacing the page data for all useContent consumers with the wrong entry. This risks failing the verification criteria that the Homepage and Discover Article pages show the changed draft entry content.
issues.suggestedFix: Track the current page's contentTypeUid/entryUid (e.g. from pageProps/contentstackConfig, as the plan's reuse of the getSinglePageEntry pattern implies) and refetch that entry in onEntryChange, rather than inferring the entry from the first [data-cslp] DOM node. At minimum, resolve the entry identity from the active page context instead of a global document query.

issues.description: previewPage state in LivePreviewProvider is never reset on route change. Once set, useContent merges { ...content, page: previewPage } for every page in the app, so after previewing the Homepage, navigating to a Discover Article page (or any other page) will continue to serve the stale Homepage preview entry as 'page' — a functional regression of the 'no preview signal active → published content unchanged' criterion for any subsequent navigation within a preview session. The key={path} remount does not help because LivePreviewProvider sits above Component and its state persists.
issues.suggestedFix: Reset previewPage to undefined on route change (subscribe to router.events 'routeChangeComplete' or watch asPath in the existing useEffect) so stale preview data cannot leak across pages.

issues.description: LivePreviewProvider reads useContext(ContentstackContext) at the _app level, where no ancestor ContentstackContext.Provider exists (pages provide their own further down the tree). 'content' is therefore always the default {} and the re-provided ContentstackContext.Provider value={effectiveContent} is dead code — it is shadowed by the page-level providers for every real consumer. This is misleading and suggests the preview pipeline flows through ContentstackContext when it actually flows only through LivePreviewContext in useContent.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the useContext(ContentstackContext) read and the ContentstackContext.Provider wrapper; keep only LivePreviewContext.Provider. The useContent hook already performs the effectiveContent merge.

issues.description: SPEC + hardcoded value: (1) The plan prescribed live_preview: { enable, preview_token }, but the installed contentstack@3.17.2 SDK's LivePreview interface is { host, management_token, enable } — 'preview_token' is not consumed by this SDK version and would silently do nothing, so the implementer's use of management_token is correct and the plan's prescribed key should be amended. (2) The fallback host 'api.contentstack.io' is a hardcoded endpoint URL literal; the SDK already defaults live_preview.host to exactly this value, so the literal is unnecessary.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the '|| "api.contentstack.io"' fallback and let the SDK default apply (or pass host only when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is set), avoiding the hardcoded URL per the project constants rule.

issues.description: SPEC (plan gap, advisory only): the plan prescribed importing the server-built Stack into _app.tsx, but services/contentstack.ts destructures credentials via `const { ... } = process?.env || {}`. Next.js does not inline non-NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars into the client bundle (and destructured process.env is never inlined), so in the browser Stack has empty api_key/delivery_token/preview token and the onEntryChange refetch cannot authenticate; the failure is then swallowed by `.catch(() => {})`. Live preview may therefore not function outside a mocked environment, and 'fixing' it by exposing the management token via NEXT_PUBLIC_ would itself be a security concern. This is a flaw in the plan of record, not the implementer's deviation from it.
issues.suggestedFix: Plan-level resolution needed: either gate the client-side refetch behind a preview-mode check that fails loudly (log on catch instead of swallowing), or route the preview refetch through a server API route so credentials stay server-side. At minimum, replace `.catch(() => {})` with a logged catch so preview failures are diagnosable.

issues.description: The promise chain ends in `.catch(() => {})`, silently discarding all fetch errors. While this does avoid an unhandled rejection (TS/strict compliance is otherwise fine — the `as any` on stackSdk carries an explanatory comment), a failed preview fetch leaves stale content with no signal, making integration issues invisible.
issues.suggestedFix: Log the error (console.error or the project's logging path) inside the catch before swallowing.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The onEntryChange handler reads entry identity from `data-cslp-content-type-uid` and `data-cslp-entry-uid` DOM attributes. Verified against the repo and the installed SDK: (a) nothing in src/ renders any data-cslp* attribute (grep for 'data-cslp' across src returns only this new code), and (b) these attribute names appear nowhere in the installed @contentstack/live-preview-utils bundle — the SDK's cslp format is a single `data-cslp` attribute whose value is `contentTypeUid.entryUid.locale`, not separate per-field attributes. Both getAttribute calls will therefore return null, the handler early-returns, and setPreviewPage is never called — so none of the preview acceptance criteria (Homepage draft, Discover Article draft, successive updates) can actually fire. The installed OnEntryChangeCallback type is `() => void` (confirmed in dist/modern/livePreview/types/onEntryChangeCallback.type.d.ts), so the callback genuinely supplies no data, but the prescribed fix was to re-fetch the changed entry via the existing Stack ContentType/Entry pattern using the page's known identity — not to invent a DOM-scrape side channel.
issues.suggestedFix: In onEntryChange, re-fetch the current page's entry directly: the page's contentTypeUid is already available (it is passed to CommonAnalytics as pageProps.contentTypeUid) and the entry uid is available from the page context/props. Call Stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Entry(entryUid).toJSON().fetch() and setPreviewPage([result]) — the same fetch shape already written below, but keyed off known page identity instead of querySelector. If DOM data is truly needed, parse the standard single `data-cslp` attribute (`contentTypeUid.entryUid.locale`) rather than the non-existent per-field attributes.

issues.description: LivePreviewProvider re-provides ContentstackContext with `effectiveContent` computed from `useContext(ContentstackContext)` at the _app level. The real ContentstackContext.Provider is set per-page in src/pages/[[...slug]].tsx (line 39) and src/pages/404.tsx (line 31), which are nested INSIDE LivePreviewProvider — so (a) the `content` read here is always the default `{}` (no provider exists above it), and (b) the re-provided value is shadowed by the deeper page-level provider for every real consumer. The entire ContentstackContext.Provider wrap, the useContext import, and the effectiveContent computation in LivePreviewProvider are dead code; the working mechanism is LivePreviewContext + the merge in useContent.
issues.suggestedFix: Delete the ContentstackContext.Provider wrapper, the `useContext(ContentstackContext)` call, and the effectiveContent computation from LivePreviewProvider; render only LivePreviewContext.Provider around children. The useContent merge (previewPage ? {...content, page: previewPage} : content) already delivers preview data to all 147+ consumers.

issues.description: The plan of record prescribed `preview_token`; the implementation uses `management_token`. Verified against the installed contentstack SDK runtime bundle: `management_token` is the key the SDK actually consumes (2 occurrences in dist/node/contentstack.js; `preview_token` appears nowhere), so the deviation is functionally correct — but the env var is named CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN while being passed as `management_token`, which will confuse future maintainers into thinking a real management (write-access) token is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a one-line comment above the live_preview block noting that the SDK's `management_token` key expects the Live Preview token (CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN), not a stack management token.

issues.description: Hardcoded fallback endpoint string 'api.contentstack.io' inline in the options object. It matches the SDK's own default (confirmed in the bundle's default config), so the fallback is redundant as well as being a hardcoded URL.
issues.suggestedFix: Either omit `host` when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST is empty (the SDK defaults to api.contentstack.io), or spread conditionally: ...(CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST ? { host: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST } : {}).

issues.description: `.catch(() => {})` silently swallows fetch failures from the preview re-fetch. There is no unhandled-rejection risk (good), but a failed preview fetch leaves the author staring at stale content with no signal.
issues.suggestedFix: Log the error at minimum: `.catch((err) => console.error('Live preview entry fetch failed', err))` — consistent with the existing debug/logHandler pattern in services/contentstack.ts.

issues.description: The `Stack as any` cast does carry an explanatory comment (acceptable per the typed-any rule), but the comment claims structural compatibility that nothing verifies. The installed package exports an IStackSdk type from @contentstack/live-preview-utils (dist/modern/index.d.ts).
issues.suggestedFix: Prefer `Stack as unknown as IStackSdk` (importing the IStackSdk type) so a future SDK upgrade produces a type error at the cast site rather than silent runtime drift.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Dead imports kept alive with `void` statements. The diff adds imports of ContentstackContext, useContent, pageService and getSingleEntry, then references them only via `void ContentstackContext; void useContent; void pageService; void getSingleEntry;` plus a spurious `export type { IContentstackContext }` re-export with a comment claiming it 'keeps the context shape aligned' — none of these are actually used by the live-preview implementation. This is not just noise: importing `services/pageService` (a server-side data fetcher) and `services/contentstack`'s getSingleEntry into _app.tsx forces that module graph into the client bundle. A more concise change meets the same acceptance criteria: delete the four unused imports, the type re-export, and the four `void` lines (~10 fewer lines). Verified against the installed packages that nothing in the working implementation depends on these imports — the provider only needs Stack, ContentstackLivePreview, LivePreviewContext, getLocaleByNextLocale and useRouter.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the unused imports (ContentstackContext, useContent, pageService, getSingleEntry), the `export type { IContentstackContext }` re-export, and all four `void ...;` statements. Keep only the imports actually consumed by LivePreviewProvider.

issues.description: The fallback `host: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST || "api.contentstack.io"` hardcodes the Live Preview REST host literal, duplicating the contentstack SDK's own built-in default (verified in the installed SDK: its default config is `live_preview: { enable: false, host: "api.contentstack.io" }`). The hardcoded string is redundant — when the env var is unset the SDK already resolves this host — and it embeds an endpoint URL as a raw literal in source.
issues.suggestedFix: Omit the host key when the env var is unset, e.g. `...(CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST ? { host: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST } : {})`, letting the SDK's merged default supply the host.

issues.description: Deviation from the plan of record (advisory, functionally equivalent): the plan prescribed adding an updater field to IContentstackContext and marked useContent.ts NO EDIT REQUIRED; the implementer instead created a parallel LivePreviewContext and edited useContent to overlay previewPage onto content.page. The approach satisfies the verification criteria — when previewPage is undefined, `effectiveContent` is the original context object (no behavioral change, published-content regression criteria preserved), and successive onEntryChange events each call setPreviewPage, satisfying the sequential-update criterion — and arguably keeps the server-set ContentstackContext pristine. Flagging only so the deviation is recorded; no change required. Note also that the plan's prescribed `live_preview: { preview_token }` key is not consumed by the installed contentstack SDK runtime — the SDK reads `management_token` (sent as the authorization header) and `host` from live_preview config, both of which the implementer used correctly; the plan's key name was wrong, the implementation is right. SPEC: the plan of record should be updated to prescribe `management_token` rather than `preview_token` for the live_preview block.
issues.suggestedFix: No code change required; optionally update the plan/spec to reflect the LivePreviewContext approach and the correct `management_token` config key.
